messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw steady KV page growth on a Dedicated customer workload over a 48h run that doesn't show up on Hosted. Memory climbs ~200MB/hr until we start evicting. Figured i'd drop initial traces here and get thoughts.
maria: Can you paste the profiler output and which model/seq lengths? :eyes:
simon: also which eviction policy are they running? LRU vs TTL makes a big diff.
alex: Model is r-instruct-v1, 8k context avg, occasional 64k spikes from a batch job. Eviction in config is `lru` but page_size is default. Attaching small sample from perf-tool:
```
KV pages resident: 6.1GB -> 8.0GB over 24h
KV pages swapped: 0
Unique KV fragments: 124k -> 321k
avg reuse window: 9.4s -> 2.1s
kernel: favoured-cu17-optim (jit)
batching: micro-batch 32 -> 16 spikes
```
kelsey: interesting that swaps=0 — indicates we're not paging to disk but fragmentation increases. might be per-request KV id churn.
maria: Does Hosted for same tenant see same pattern when using hosted endpoint? alex: Hosted flatlines at ~5.8GB and fragments are ~110k, reuse window ~11s.
simon: Could be config drift. Private/Dedicated customers often have `max_resident_kv_bytes` higher and `page_size` left default which increases fragmentation. Also VPC deployments sometimes disable the shared memory segment for KV IPC -> fallback to memcpy which increases memory copies and temporary fragmentation.
chris: We saw similar on-prem issue last month where old NVIDIA driver caused fallback to software pinned allocations; growth came from failed reuse of preallocated KV buffers.
ops-bot: NOTE: customer 'acme-corp' Dedicated cluster is on kernel 5.15 and cuda 12.0; Hosted runs cuda 12.3, kernel 6.x.
alex: Good catch. So differences: kernel/driver, IPC/shm settings from VPC, eviction config drift, and batching changes. Also the runtime's kernel selection may be picking a kernel variant that uses per-token scratch buffers that aren't returned to the KV pool quickly for long sequences.
maria: Any quick mitigation for Dedicated customers? reduce max_resident_kv_bytes? switch eviction_policy to 'ttl' for heavy long-context streams?
simon: Quick mitigations to test:
- temporarily decrease page_size (e.g. 64MB -> 16MB) to reduce fragmentation footprint
- enable aggressive TTL evictions for streams flagged as long-context
- force kernel variant with smaller per-token scratch (env override: RW_KERNEL_PREFER_SMALL_SCRATCH=1)
- align batching heuristics: avoid mixing 64k spikes with 512 prompt bursts (use bucketed batching)
kelsey: we should also add a telemetry tag to trace per-deployment kv_alloc/reuse rates. Right now we only aggregate.
alex: added a debug flag to customer's Dedicated in trial: `kv.debug_tag=kv_dedicated_acme_1769` — collecting 6h trace now.
perf-bot: perf regression alert linked: RH-2345 (kv-frag-dedicated) — rolling window shows +12% p50 tail on token generation since kernel switch.
maria: If we confirm it's config drift, ops should provide a recommended `redwoodctl` patch for Dedicated/Private customers. Something like:
```
redwoodctl set cluster acme-corp --kv.page_size=16MB --kv.eviction=ttl --kv.max_resident_kv_bytes=6GB
```
chris: For on-prem: advise upgrade cuda driver to 12.3+ and enable /dev/shm sized to >16GB (VPC images sometimes set it low), also check `sysctl vm.max_map_count` for large-mmap workloads.
alex: One more datapoint from the 6h trace:
```
per-req kv_writes/sec: host=12.2, dedicated=45.1
avg kv_frag_size: host=8KB, dedicated=2KB
reuse_window_ms histogram: host: median 11000, dedicated median 2100
```
maria: That kv_writes/sec difference is huge — implies batching heuristics creating many short-lived KV objects on Dedicated.
simon: Could be our micro-batching policy for Dedicated that tries to reduce latency by splitting into smaller sub-batches. That increases KV churn. We can revert to the Hosted batching policy for Dedicated as an experiment.
kelsey: Action items:
- alex to share 24h full trace link (in #secure) and open a ticket RH-2356 for telemetry enhancements
- simon to run kernel selection A/B on a canary Dedicated node (force older kernel variant)
- ops to validate /dev/shm and driver versions on customer's fleet
- maria to draft redwoodctl recommended config
alex: sounds good. tagging @simon @maria @ops-bot. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
perf-bot: summary: KV fragmentation + high write churn on Dedicated tied to batching policy + kernel/driver differences + config drift. Recommend telemetry, conservative eviction, and batching alignment as next steps.
